transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Start time: 15:00 UTC 
Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Acacia Head of ML), Tom Lang (Acacia Platform), Sara Kline (Acacia Product)

Summary:
- Weekly POC sync focused on recent regression bump after prompt set extension; triaged candidate causes (model variant, prompt drift, scoring thresholds, guardrail false positives).
- Agreed next steps: run regression sweep, prioritize failing prompts, tune thresholds, schedule perf sweep across smaller/larger model variants.

Topics discussed:
- Recent quality drop: when it started and which user flows are impacted
- Prompt set expansion and scoring rubric changes from last week
- Guardrail false positives vs true violations and how to reduce noise
- Quick performance/latency tradeoffs for 2.7B vs 13B variants
- Security/compliance question re: Private deployment and audit logs

Action items (captured in metadata above) reproduced here for in-call clarity.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm gonna kick us off — quick rollcall?
[00:08] Priya (Acacia): hey, priya here — we're good, thanks.
[00:10] Tom (Acacia): tom on the call.
[00:12] Sara (Acacia): sara present.
[00:14] Diego (Redwood SE): diego here, ready to dig in.
[00:18] Maya: great. so objective today: triage the uptick in failing cases after you extended the prompt catalog on monday. we'll try to isolate root cause — is it prompt drift, model variant mismatch, scoring thresholds, or guardrail noise.
[00:32] Priya: yeah, we saw a spike in regressions mostly on the clinical summarization flow — like more hallucinations and occasionally truncated outputs — which is odd since we didn't touch the model. we did add ~3k prompt templates.
[00:45] Diego: okay quick q — when you added the templates, did you also change the scoring weight for the fidelity metric?
[00:52] Priya: mm, yes we bumped fidelity weight from 0.6 to 0.75 last week in the eval harness.
[00:57] Sara: and we also enabled the new reranker for the top-k candidate selection.
[01:02] Maya: ah — so there are three moving parts: new prompts, new scoring weights, and reranker on top. all could interact.
[01:12] Tom: i can share the CI artifacts — logs and the eval diff — we uploaded to the shared drive, link in the calendar note.
[01:19] Maya: perfect, i'll pull that after. Diego, maybe we start with a targeted regression sweep — 2k examples that cover the clinical summarization and diagnostic Q&A flows?
[01:28] Diego: yep that's what i had in mind. i'll run the sweep across the current production variant (13B) and a smaller 2.7B to see if it's model capacity related. also flip reranker on/off to see contribution.
[01:40] Priya: are we expecting latency to blow out on 13B? we need to keep roundtrip under 600ms in the UI.
[01:47] Diego: depends on concurrency and batching; on Redwood Dedicated we've seen median around 420ms for 13B with the current batching config, but that was warm. 2.7B sits in 200–260ms. (note: numbers rough)
[02:00] Sara: so if the 2.7B is acceptable quality-wise that could save a lot of cost.
[02:04] Priya: cost is definitely a factor but fidelity is the priority for clinical outputs.
[02:09] Maya: right, which is why the eval weighting matters. Priya, when you bumped fidelity to 0.75, what happened to recall-based fail modes?
[02:18] Priya: recall dropped a touch — some shorter answers got cut, which led the guardrail to mark them as incomplete. also some semantic paraphrases were flagged as low fidelity because the metric expects n-gram overlap.
[02:31] Diego: that's metric brittleness — we need to include paraphrase-tolerant metrics (e.g., BERTscore or embedding sim) in the eval mix.
[02:38] Tom: we can add BERTscore, but it will change the baseline numbers — is Redwood comfortable with a composite metric?
[02:44] Maya: yes, we frequently recommend a composite: lexical + semantic + domain-specific checks. Diego, could you propose a composite and show expected deltas?
[02:52] Diego: will do. i'll include BERTscore, an embedding-sim threshold, and keep a smaller n-gram overlap. i'll run both the old and new metric on the 2k set.
[03:03] Priya: on guardrails — many of the false positives are around benign medical phrasing that the safety filter flags as 'advice'.
[03:12] Sara: yeah, e.g., "if symptoms persist seek care" gets flagged even when we asked for differential diagnosis.
[03:18] Diego: are the guardrails rule-based or model-based?
[03:21] Priya: rule-based mostly, with a small ML layer for intent detection.
[03:26] Maya: we should adjust thresholding to reduce noise: tune guardrail sensitivity and add a whitelist for clinical templates that are explicitly allowed.
[03:35] Tom: whitelist would help; we can annotate which prompt templates are allowed to include clinical advice phrasing.
[03:40] Priya: good, we'll start a whitelist and share it.
[03:44] Maya: perfect. moving on — there were a couple of anomalous truncations in the logs — Diego, you saw those?
[03:50] Diego: yes, one case shows we hit token limit because the prompt expansion added extra context; that caused early stop. we can either increase max tokens for those flows or compact the context.
[04:02] Priya: compacting context is preferable if it preserves fidelity — increasing token limit can raise cost.
[04:08] Diego: agreed. i can run an experiment that collapses redundant context items and compares output quality.
[04:14] Maya: thanks. quick note on deployments — Acacia asked last week about Private options for audit logs and KMS. any updates?
[04:22] Maya: (continues) we circulated an initial security note in the CRM thread; i'll attach SOC2 scope and KMS integration notes after this call.
[04:30] Priya: please, we need to show to internal compliance.
[04:33] Maya: yep i'll do that.
[04:35] Sara: one more question on fallbacks — if we detect low-confidence outputs should we fallback to a canned response or re-run with a larger model?
[04:44] Diego: both are options. re-run with larger model increases cost/latency; canned response keeps latency low but affects UX. another approach: run a quick reranker or calibration step that uses a small discriminator to estimate hallucination risk.
[04:58] Priya: we prefer re-run for high-risk flows, canned responses for low-risk. we should define risk tiers.
[05:05] Maya: agreed — let's define 3 risk tiers and map fallback behavior. Sara, can you draft the mapping?
[05:11] Sara: yes i'll draft and share by friday.
[05:14] Diego: back to regression triage plan — i'll run five experiments: (1) baseline 13B current config, (2) 13B without reranker, (3) 2.7B with reranker, (4) 2.7B without reranker, (5) 13B with compacted context.
[05:29] Priya: that sounds comprehensive. include the eval metric delta for each.
[05:33] Diego: will do. expect results in 48–72 hours depending on queue.
[05:37] Maya: great. any blockers on your side, Priya?
[05:40] Priya: only that we need to label the 25 top failures so we can triage root causes faster. i'll get the team to pull that list and send it over.
[05:49] Tom: also, we'll share one infra log for a truncation case — that should help Diego debug the tokenization path.
[05:55] Maya: perfect.
[05:57] (brief pause / file shuffling noise)
[06:05] Sara: small note — a stakeholder asked about competitor behavior; wonder if OpenAI autoprompting would behave differently in this flow?
[06:14] Diego: likely yes but we shouldn't benchmark blind. if you'd like, we can run a controlled head-to-head on a tiny sample.
[06:21] Priya: not necessary yet; first want to stabilize internal baseline.
[06:25] Maya: OK. next, scoring weight discussion — Priya, can you confirm you want fidelity prioritized for clinical flows only?
[06:33] Priya: yes, clinical flows fidelity 0.75, other flows keep 0.6.
[06:38] Diego: i'll build the eval split by flow and compute per-flow metrics.
[06:42] Maya: excellent. scheduling: we will reconvene after Diego's sweep and once the 25 prompts are labeled; is next Wednesday good?
[06:50] Priya: next wed is fine.
[06:52] Tom: fine.
[06:53] Sara: yep.
[06:54] Maya: ok, restate next steps quickly — diego runs the 2k regression across five experiments, priya sends 25 flagged prompts, sara drafts risk->fallback mapping, maya shares security docs and SOC2 notes, tom sends infra log.
[07:10] Priya: sounds right.
[07:12] Diego: one more technical note — i'll include embedding sim thresholds and a proposed composite metric with expected deltas.
[07:20] Maya: all right, wrapping up — any last questions?
[07:23] Tom: can you also double-check retention policy for the debug logs? compliance asked for 1 year.
[07:29] Maya: yes i'll confirm and put it in the CRM thread.
[07:33] Priya: thanks, appreciate it.
[07:35] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in the thread and send an updated action-item tracker.
[07:42] (meeting ends)

Post-call notes (auto-gen may have small errors):
- Diego to attach CSV with per-prompt scores and diffs; include reranker on/off flags.
- Customer to classify failing prompts by failure mode: hallucination, truncation, guardrail false-positive, low-recall.
- Consider adding an embedding similarity threshold to reduce metric brittleness around paraphrases.
- Discussed Private/KMS options; Maya will share security artifact.

References / links mentioned during call:
